Five full-service branches: two moderate-, one middle-, two upper-income tracts. Giving is from the limited-scope facts table: Donations 6 / $20 thousand.
mechanics_bank_bakersfield.pe_giving: 6 donations totaling $20,000 in the Bakersfield assessment area (PE limited-scope facts table), alongside 1 new investment of $1.7M and 11 community development loans totaling $14.0M
mechanics_bank_bakersfield.pe_need_quote: The Service Test is rated “Low-Satisfactory.” The bank’s performance in California is consistent with this rating
mechanics_bank_bakersfield.documented_gap: The AA-level finding is sharper than the institution rating and points the OTHER way. Institution-wide Mechanics is Investment Outstanding / Service Low Satisfactory. But the PE's limited-scope summary table rates the Investment Test 'Bakersfield' assessment area as BELOW the institution's overall performance — one of ten California AAs marked Below on investments. So in this county the investment side is the weak one, against an Outstanding institution-wide rating. Both tests our activity feeds are therefore in play here. Institution-wide the Service Test is Low Satisfactory.
mechanics_bank_bakersfield.cluster_role: Kern — the only pressured bank with the county in a delineated assessment area, but a POOL candidate at $20,000 of three-year AA giving.
mechanics_bank_bakersfield.cofunder_consent_note: Ask at signing. Default is a count, never a name — CD grants are not in the public CRA file.

meridian_bank.name: Meridian Bank
meridian_bank.aa_note: (the assessment area also covers Burlington, Camden, Gloucester and Salem Counties in New Jersey, New Castle County in Delaware and Cecil County in Maryland — 11 counties across four states in ONE assessment area. Only the five Pennsylvania counties are listed here; no figures are produced for any of them, see artifact_status.)
meridian_bank.aa_structure: ONE assessment area spanning FOUR states: 'a single assessment area consisting of 11 contiguous counties' comprising the Philadelphia-Camden-Wilmington, PA-NJ-DE-MD MSA in its entirety — Burlington/Camden/Gloucester (NJ), Bucks/Chester/Montgomery (PA), Delaware/Philadelphia (PA), and New Castle (DE)/Cecil (MD)/Salem (NJ). Because it is a single AA, institution-wide giving IS assessment-area giving — there is no per-AA allocation question.
meridian_bank.component_ratings: Lending High Satisfactory / Investment LOW SATISFACTORY / Service LOW SATISFACTORY — overall Satisfactory
meridian_bank.ask_basis: anchored on disclosed giving in the TARGET assessment area — trivially so, because the bank has only ONE assessment area, so its institution-wide donation total IS its assessment-area total: 65 donations totaling $511,526.
meridian_bank.ask_sizing: sized by src/ask.py: $170,509/yr in the single assessment area x 15% x 1.25 = $31,970 -> $25,000 (earmark, at the ceiling). CAVEAT: the $511,526 is '65 donations or educational improvement tax credits (EITCs)'. EITCs are a Pennsylvania tax-credit programme, not straight grants, so the donation-only figure is lower by an unstated amount and this ask sits at the optimistic end.
meridian_bank.verify_note: Verified 2026-08-25 from the Nov 29, 2022 FDIC public evaluation. The PE delineates: 'Bank designates a single assessment area consisting of 11 contiguous counties … Burlington, Camden, and Gloucester Counties in the Camden, NJ Metropolitan Division #15804; Bucks, Chester, and Montgomery Counties in the Montgomery County-Bucks County-Chester County, PA Metropolitan Division #33874; Delaware and Philadelphia Counties in the Philadelphia, PA Metropolitan Division #37964; and New Castle, Cecil, and Salem Counties in the Wilmington, DE-MD-NJ Metropolitan Division #48864.' RESOLVES a 2022-vintage corrupt row: the API reported BOTH Investment and Service as 'Substantial Non Complianc'; the PE states both are Low Satisfactory.
meridian_bank.pe_giving: 65 donations or educational improvement tax credits totaling $511,526, within 76 qualified investments totaling $13.3M — single assessment area, so this is the AA figure
meridian_bank.pe_need_quote: Meridian Bank has an adequate level of qualified community development investments and grants. The bank is rarely in a leadership position
meridian_bank.documented_gap: BOTH tests our activity feeds are Low Satisfactory. The assessment area contains PHILADELPHIA COUNTY — the 18th largest SNAP enrollment gap in the country — which is precisely the county our data cannot currently quantify.
meridian_bank.cluster_role: Philadelphia — blocked. Strongest evidence of any blocked bank in the roster.
meridian_bank.cofunder_consent_note: Ask at signing. Default is a count, never a name — CD grants are not in the public CRA file.
meridian_bank.artifact_note: Buildable in COVERAGE mode only. This assessment area spans four states and no state's gross-income fact base can support an absolute claim across it — PA and NJ carry FNS-divergence CAUTIONs and DE and MD have no fact base at all. The national coverage index covers all eleven counties, so the artifact ranks them and states no gap size and no dollar figure. See src/coverage.py.
meridian_bank.public_file_check: PUBLIC-FILE CHECK 2026-08-25: NO CRA CONTENT on meridianbanker.com/community — the word CRA does not appear. Main line (866) 327-9199. Their assessment area therefore cannot be re-checked against a current public file; the Nov 2022 PE remains the only source.

firstrust_savings_bank.name: Firstrust Savings Bank
firstrust_savings_bank.aa_note: (Camden County, New Jersey is part of this assessment area and is ranked with it; the bank's separate Lehigh County PA and Towson MD assessment areas are excluded)
firstrust_savings_bank.aa_structure: THREE assessment areas: Philadelphia PA-NJ Multistate MSA (targeted — Bucks, Chester, Delaware, Montgomery and Philadelphia in PA plus Camden in NJ), Lehigh County PA, and Towson MD (census tracts in Baltimore County, added when the Towson branch opened in Aug 2020). Do NOT merge.
firstrust_savings_bank.component_ratings: Lending Low Satisfactory / Investment LOW SATISFACTORY / Service LOW SATISFACTORY
firstrust_savings_bank.ask_basis: anchored on disclosed giving in the TARGET assessment area: 122 grants and donations totaling nearly $8.9 million that the PE says 'specifically benefitted this assessment area' — the Philadelphia PA-NJ Multistate MSA. Institution-wide giving is $9.4M across three assessment areas and is deliberately not used.
firstrust_savings_bank.ask_sizing: sized by src/ask.py: $2,966,667/yr in the Philadelphia assessment area x 15% x 1.25 = $556,250 -> $25,000 (earmark, at the ceiling)
firstrust_savings_bank.verify_note: Verified 2026-08-25 from the Nov 6, 2023 FDIC public evaluation. The PE delineates the target assessment area: 'Philadelphia-Camden-Wilmington, PA-NJ-Delaware (DE)-Maryland (MD) Metropolitan Statistical Area … includes Bucks, Chester, Delaware, Montgomery, and Philadelphia Counties in PA, and Camden County in NJ.' All three tests are Low Satisfactory. Found by pricing the severe-gap subset of the national pressure universe, not by county search.
firstrust_savings_bank.pe_giving: 122 grants and donations totaling nearly $8.9 million specifically benefitting the Philadelphia PA-NJ Multistate MSA assessment area, within 142 qualified investments, donations and EITCs totaling $17.7M there. Institution-wide giving is $9.4M plus $735,000 of EITCs.
firstrust_savings_bank.pe_need_quote: Firstrust has a significant level of qualified community development investments and grants within the Philadelphia, PA-NJ Multistate MSA, occasionally in a leadership position
firstrust_savings_bank.documented_gap: ALL THREE tests are Low Satisfactory — the only bank in the roster where that is true. Both tests our activity feeds are gapped.
firstrust_savings_bank.cluster_role: Philadelphia — a second, independent route into the #18 county alongside Meridian, with far larger disclosed assessment-area giving ($8.9M against Meridian's $511,526).
firstrust_savings_bank.cofunder_consent_note: Ask at signing. Default is a count, never a name — CD grants are not in the public CRA file.

commonwealth_business_bank.name: Commonwealth Business Bank
commonwealth_business_bank.aa_structure: THREE rated areas: California (Los Angeles-Orange, targeted), Texas (Dallas) and one other. Do NOT merge — Dallas separately received $52,500 against Los Angeles-Orange's $215,500.
commonwealth_business_bank.component_ratings: Lending Low Satisfactory / Investment LOW SATISFACTORY / Service LOW SATISFACTORY
commonwealth_business_bank.ask_basis: anchored on disclosed giving in the TARGET assessment area: '$215,500 in qualified community development donations impacting this assessment area' — the Los Angeles-Orange assessment area. Their Dallas assessment area separately received $52,500, which is why the anchor must name its area.
commonwealth_business_bank.ask_sizing: sized by src/ask.py: $71,833/yr in the Los Angeles-Orange assessment area x 15% x 1.25 = $13,469 -> $12,500 (earmark)
commonwealth_business_bank.verify_note: Verified 2026-08-25 from the Sep 23, 2024 Federal Reserve public evaluation. The PE states 'The Los Angeles-Orange assessment area consists of Los Angeles and Orange Counties in their entirety'. All three tests are rated Low Satisfactory. FDIC cert is 57873, confirmed via BankFind by RSSD 3337097 after the liveness gate rejected a guessed number. Found by reading the severe-gap subset of the national pressure universe. CAUTION recorded: the bank's OTHER donation figure, $52,500, belongs to its DALLAS assessment area — reading that as the Los Angeles figure would understate the anchor fourfold.
commonwealth_business_bank.pe_giving: $215,500 in qualified community development donations impacting the Los Angeles-Orange assessment area, alongside 14 investments totaling $5.1 million that directly benefit it
commonwealth_business_bank.pe_need_quote: exhibited a poor responsiveness to community development needs through investments in this area
commonwealth_business_bank.documented_gap: ALL THREE tests Low Satisfactory. In the Los Angeles-Orange assessment area the PE additionally finds the bank 'exhibited a poor responsiveness to community development needs through investments' — harsher than the rating.
commonwealth_business_bank.cluster_role: Los Angeles — a fourth route into the #1 county alongside Hanmi, CTBC and City National.
commonwealth_business_bank.cofunder_consent_note: Ask at signing. Default is a count, never a name — CD grants are not in the public CRA file.

woodforest_houston.name: Woodforest National Bank
woodforest_houston.aa_note: (Houston CSA: Houston-The Woodlands-Sugar Land MSA plus non-metro Matagorda, Walker, Washington and Wharton)
woodforest_houston.aa_structure: one of 25 rating areas; Houston CSA taken for full-scope review in Texas
woodforest_houston.component_ratings: Lending Outstanding / Investment Outstanding / Service Outstanding (institution); Texas Investment Outstanding, Service Outstanding
woodforest_houston.pe_giving: Houston CSA: 111 total investment allocations totaling $117.5 million, of which 36 GRANTS totaling $17.8 million. Scope verified: the figure sits inside the 'Houston CSA' investment section. Other AAs are two to three orders of magnitude smaller (Charleston $14,433; Charlotte $56,849), which is exactly the pattern that has produced wrong-AA errors here before.
woodforest_houston.documented_gap: none — Outstanding on all three tests. Included on CAPACITY, not pressure. This bank was excluded by the old gap-only screen by construction; see docs/strategy/targeting-thesis-challenge-2026-08-25.md.
woodforest_houston.ask_sizing: peer path: capacity anchor with no gap multiplier (PEER_MULTIPLIER=1.0). $17.8M over 4 years x 15% far exceeds the $25,000 ceiling, so the ask is the ceiling.
woodforest_houston.ask_basis: 36 grants totaling $17.8 million disclosed for the Houston CSA
woodforest_houston.verify_note: Identity confirmed via FDIC BankFind: cert 23220, RSSD 412751, TX, $8.98B, active. AA counties and the $17.8M grant figure read from the May 22, 2023 OCC PE (charter 16892); ratings read from the narrative rather than the X-grid, which pdftotext flattens unreliably.
